title: Concept type
description: Which group a concept belongs to. A separate record rather than a field on the concept, because the concept was signed by one person on one date and the typing is a second judgement by possibly another — writing it into the signed record would put unsigned content inside a signature (ADR-0071). The four groups the owner ruled on (OQ-0001) sort a concept by the part it plays in reasoning towards a decision; the five added on 2026-09-09 sort it by the part it plays in the process that reasoning sits inside (ADR-0098). Shape only: which group a concept belongs in is a legal judgement, and since ADR-0079 an agent may propose one provided the proposal is stamped unreviewed.

concept.description: The approved concept this types, by its GC- id. The harness reports a type record naming a concept that is not in the gold set as a dangling cross-reference.

type.description: The group. Four sort a concept by the part it plays in reasoning towards a decision, and they are the owner's own (OQ-0001): `ground_of_refusal` — a reason an application can be refused. `legal_test` — a question the decision maker has to answer. `relevant_factor` — something that feeds into that answer. `exception` — something that takes a case out of the rule. Five sort a concept by the part it plays in the process that reasoning sits inside, and they exist because 53 of 130 concepts fitted none of the first four (ADR-0098): `process_role` — a person or body that acts. `subject_matter` — the thing the process operates on. `procedural_step` — an act, proceeding or event that moves an application or a registration from one state to the next. `instrument_or_record` — a document, entry or endorsement the process produces, or writes to the Register. `external_instrument` — a treaty or international scheme Australian practice adopts, rather than a rule the Act itself makes. `none_of_these` is an answer too, and a real one: it says none of the nine fit this concept, which is evidence about the taxonomy rather than a gap in the data.

basis.description: The passages the typing rests on, by upstream ref. Optional, because a person who knows the domain may type a concept from knowledge rather than from a passage — but a typing with a basis can be checked and one without cannot, and the coverage report counts the difference.
